title: Payer Readiness for January 1: Testing Claims Before 2027 CPT Goes Live
summary: Test claims before 2027 CPT goes live. Learn how to check payer readiness, clearinghouse edits and billing workflows before January 1.

Payer readiness for 2027 CPT decides whether January claims get paid or stall at the clearinghouse. The 2027 CPT code set applies to dates of service on or after January 1, 2027. Use the remaining time to check that every system in your billing process supports the new codes. This post is a testing plan:


- What to test

## Why Payer Readiness for 2027 CPT Matters Before Go-Live


The AMA publishes the CPT code set, but it doesn’t load it into anyone’s system. Each payer, clearinghouse, and claim scrubber updates its own code tables on its own schedule. A code can be valid in the 2027 CPT book and still be rejected because one link in the chain hasn’t caught up.


Deleted codes cause a different problem. Once the new code set applies, deleted codes are invalid for dates of service on or after January 1, 2027, even if your charge master or superbill still lists them.


In both ways, the result is the same: rejections that need rework, claim denials that need appeals, and cash that arrives weeks late. These delays affect cash flow early in the year, when patient balances take longer to collect.


## What Payers and Clearinghouses Update: 2027 CPT Payer Edits


Before a new code pays cleanly, several pieces must change on the payer side:


- **Code tables:** new and revised codes added, deleted codes end-dated.


- **Fee schedules:** a rate assigned to each new code.


- **Claim edits:** bundling, modifier, and frequency rules for the new codes.


- **Prior authorization rules:** updated code lists for services that need approval.


- **Medical policies:** coverage criteria that name specific codes.


Payers update their systems at different times, sometimes they announce changes just weeks before January. Focus on the busiest code areas in the 2027 update, such as


**\[code area 1\]** and


**\[code area 2\]** , where new or revised codes may trigger unexpected edits.


## How to Test Claims Before January 1


If you’re working out how to test claims before new CPT codes take effect, run these four steps in order. Each one catches a different kind of failure.


#### 1. Build a Test Claim Set from Your Highest-Volume Changes


Pull your top codes by volume and revenue, then match them against the new, revised, and deleted codes in the 2027 set. Build a small set of test claims that covers each type: a new code, a revised code, and a claim that still carries a deleted code. Add the modifier combinations your team bills most.


#### 2. Run It Through Your Scrubber and Practice Management System


Confirm that your claim scrubber vendor has loaded the 2027 rules, then run the test set through the scrubber and your practice management system. The deleted code should fail, and the new and revised codes should pass with the right fee schedule amount. Anything else is a fix to make in December, not January.


#### 3. Ask Each Major Payer and Your Clearinghouse What Testing They Support


Many payers don’t offer production testing for new codes, so don’t assume you can send a test claim. Ask your top payers and your clearinghouse when 2027 codes load, what testing they support, and where updates will be posted. If no testing option is available, submit a small batch of claims in early January and review the results before sending the rest.


#### 4. Check Authorizations That Span January 1


Authorizations approved in 2026 may list codes that are revised or deleted in 2027. Review open authorizations for services scheduled after January 1 and ask the payer whether they need an update. A valid code on a mismatched authorization can still be denied.

## Medicare Timing to Watch


CMS released the CY 2027 Physician Fee Schedule final rule (CMS-1848-F) on November 4, 2026, after the July 14 proposed rule (CMS-1848-P). The final rule is effective January 1, 2027, so its policies are now final, not proposed. See the


CMS final rule fact sheet


and the


Federal Register notice


.


One important change for coding teams includes modifier 25. CMS finalized a payment reduction for office or outpatient E/M visits billed on the same day as a 0-day global procedure by the same practice. Use the final rule, not the July proposal, and update your Medicare fee schedule before submitting January claims.


## 2027 CPT Go-Live Checklist


Use this list to confirm your team is ready to test claims before January 1 and release them cleanly after.


- **Code tables loaded:** new and revised 2027 CPT codes added and deleted codes end-dated in your practice management system and charge master.


- **Claim scrubber update for new CPT codes:** vendor confirms new codes, revised descriptors, and deleted-code edits are live.


- **Fee schedules updated:** rates loaded for each major payer, including the final Medicare fee schedule.


- **Test claims run:** test set passed through the scrubber and practice management system, with failures fixed.


- **Payer answers in writing:** load dates and testing options saved for each major payer and the clearinghouse.


- **Open authorizations reviewed:** open authorizations for January services checked against 2027 codes.


- **Templates updated:** superbills, order sets, and EHR templates show current codes only.


- **Staff briefed:** coders, billers, and front desk know the changes and the day-one plan.


## Day-One Monitoring Plan


For the first two weeks of January, review claims daily instead of weekly. Problems caught on day two cost far less than problems found at month-end.


- **Rejections:** clearinghouse rejections by code and payer to spot a code that isn’t loaded.


- **Denials by payer:** a cluster of denials on one new code usually means a missing fee schedule or payer to edit.


- **Claims held** check scrubber holds daily, so clean claims don’t sit behind one bad rule.


- **Daily review owner:** name one person who reviews all three reports every morning.


- **Escalation path:** decide now who contacts the payer rep, the clearinghouse, and the scrubber vendor, and how fast.


Fix the root cause before resubmitting a batch, so the same edit doesn’t reject every claim it affects.

## FAQ


#### 1. When should practices start testing claims for 2027 CPT changes?


Start testing in December, once your practice management system, clearinghouse, and claim scrubber have loaded the 2027 updates. Complete testing before January 1 to identify coding errors, missing fee schedules, and claim edits before live claims go out.


#### 2. Will payers accept new CPT codes on January 1, 2027?


Not necessarily. Payers update their systems on different schedules, so a new CPT code may be valid but not yet recognized by a payer’s system. Confirm code availability and testing requirements with your major payers before submitting claims.


#### 3. What should practices include in their CPT test claims?


Include new, revised, and deleted codes, along with commonly billed modifier combinations. Prioritize high-volume services, and codes that have the greatest impact on revenue to catch errors before go-live.


#### 4. What happens if a payer has not loaded the new CPT codes?


Claims may be rejected or denied because the payer cannot recognize the code or apply the correct edits. Confirm the payer’s expected update date, document its response, and follow its submission guidance until the codes are available.


#### 5. How can practices prevent claim denials from 2027 CPT changes?


Update code tables, fee schedules, authorization requirements ad claim scrubber rules before January. Test claims, review open authorizatins, and monitor rejections and denials daily during the first two weeks of January to identify and correct issues quickly.
